analysis:
The change touches docs/architecture/inference.md only. Two units were supplied as BASE text: the Two-Mac cluster, Flint and related sections. The patch excerpt is truncated, and the head-side hunks near head lines 3528-3536, 5230-5235, 5250-5284, 5291-5294 and 5370-5372 were not visible to me beyond the excerpt.

What the patch shows: (1) the header date moves to 2026-10-31. (2) A paragraph is added at head ~3528-3536 saying the cluster service writes its heartbeat to the file named by DARKBLOOM_CLUSTER_MEMBER_HEALTH_FILE (service-health.json). The supervisor's liveness guard accepts only a beat carrying the service's own PID, and ClusterService.partEnvironment gives this Mac's part a different file (part-health.json) so the part never overwrites the service heartbeat. (3) The 'Cluster runtime facts' section now says a signed release computes cluster-runtime digests from its own final app and registers them as `cluster_runtime`.

Security relevance: these are documentation-only changes. No executable code, key custody, coordinator wire protocol or sandbox boundary is altered in the visible evidence. The health-file separation is a liveness/availability matter. The PID check limits spoofing of liveness by a part, which is consistent with TB-003 and T-043 (the watchdog is the same replaceable binary). The release-time digest registration touches the A-017/T-054 qualification-identity area, but it is only described, not implemented here. I cannot verify the described behavior in the release lane or the Swift sources, which are outside the supplied evidence.

Open integration questions: (a) whether the release lane's `cluster_runtime` registration is authenticated by the existing release API key (A-005); (b) whether the health-file env var could be attacker-set by a same-UID process (T-060-style local DoS). Neither is evidenced as a regression.

No findings.
